verdict.rationale: Parahelp documents a Releases system: configuration actions approved from Internal Agent tasks, which include automations, publish as releases that are 'reviewed, versioned, and revertable' with one-click revert. Per-action manual approval by default gives a review step. However, the evidence covers versioning of the configuration changes automations produce, not versioning or rollback of the automation definitions themselves (schedule, trigger, prompt). missing for 10: documented version history and rollback of automation definitions, diff view for automation changes, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: approving a configuration action publishes it as a release - reviewed, versioned, and revertable
Configuration actions publish as a release on the Releases page, where you can track the impact and revert with one click.
By default, every action requires manual approval. You can set specific tools to auto-approve per task or automation
An automation is an Internal Agent task that runs on a schedule
